source_audit: R1796 formalizes continuous weak-BSG selection following the mechanism of Tao, Product set estimates for non-commutative groups, arXiv math/0601431v3, Lemma5.1 (primary source read in R1795; https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0601431). The new proof directly derives simultaneous size and low-codegree control using Cauchy–Schwarz, Tonelli and a positive finite weighted-averaging margin. It uses the relaxed size H(S)>H(A)/(2K), with strict exceptional-pair bound, and defines D as a global popular quotient region to reuse R1795 topology and Markov bounds. Its support and volume are quantitative. The self-energy corollary supplies H(S)>H(O)/(4L), H(D)<=32L^4 H(O)/epsilon and explicit entry boxes. These are supporting formalizations of a known mechanism, not novelty claims or new impossibility theorems. Full small-product BSG, approximate-group extraction, growth/escape and strict flattening remain unproved.

proof_scope: In progress. R1796 proves continuous weak-BSG selection. From product-pair measure at least H(A)H(B)/K it selects an actual fiber S={a in A:ab in C} with H(S)>H(A)/(2K), and a global popular quotient region D. Fewer than epsilon H(S)^2 pairs in S x S have aa'^-1 outside D, and epsilon H(B)H(D)<=2K^2 H(C)^2. S,D are nonempty open precompact for the bounded open SL2 inputs, with explicit entry bounds. A checked self-energy corollary gives S subset O with H(S)>H(O)/(4L), H(D)<=32L^4 H(O)/epsilon, the same exceptional-pair bound, and closure bounds Box(Q), Box(8Q^4). This closes the full simultaneous selection target, not just its moment bookkeeping. Full small-product BSG, approximate-group extraction, metric transfer, SL2 growth/escape, strict flattening and unconditional paid padding remain unproved.
